req.title: Return 405 for unsupported /players root method
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when using DELETE on /players/ (collection).

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-036 requires HTTP 405 when DELETE is issued against the /players/ collection root. The SUT defines DELETE only at /players/squadnumber/{squad_number}, not at /players/. Three tests are needed: (1) a negative/EP test confirming DELETE /players/ returns exactly 405; (2) a boundary/BVA test confirming the Allow header lists the actually-supported methods on /players/ (POST, GET) and not DELETE, catching constant/string mutations; (3) a state-transition/STC test confirming that a valid DELETE on the specific sub-resource /players/squadnumber/1 still returns 204 (proving the router distinguishes the two paths and the 405 is path-specific, not a global DELETE ban). Together these kill status-code constant mutations (405->404, 405->400), Allow-header content mutations, and path-routing mutations.

tests.name: test_delete_players_root_returns_405
preconditions: No DELETE route is registered for /players/ collection
actions: Send HTTP DELETE to /players/ using TestClient
expected: Response status code is not 200, 204, 404, or 400
trace: R-PLAYER-036: system shall respond with HTTP 405 when using DELETE on /players/ (collection)
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_players_root_returns_405():
    client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
    response = client.delete('/players/')
    assert response.status_code == 405, (
        f'Expected 405 but got {response.status_code}'
    )
    assert response.status_code != 200
    assert response.status_code != 204
    assert response.status_code != 404
    assert response.status_code != 400

test_delete_players_root_returns_405()

tests.name: test_delete_players_root_allow_header_excludes_delete
preconditions: DELETE /players/ is not a registered route
actions: Send HTTP DELETE to /players/ using TestClient
expected: Allow header is present in the response
trace: R-PLAYER-036: 405 response must advertise supported methods via Allow header
RFC 7231 §6.5.5: 405 response MUST include Allow header
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_players_root_allow_header_excludes_delete():
    client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
    response = client.delete('/players/')
    assert response.status_code == 405
    allow_header = response.headers.get('allow', '')
    assert allow_header != '', 'Allow header must be present on 405'
    allow_upper = allow_header.upper()
    assert 'DELETE' not in allow_upper, (
        f'DELETE must not appear in Allow header: {allow_header}'
    )
    assert 'GET' in allow_upper, (
        f'GET must appear in Allow header: {allow_header}'
    )
    assert 'POST' in allow_upper, (
        f'POST must appear in Allow header: {allow_header}'
    )

test_delete_players_root_allow_header_excludes_delete()

tests.name: test_delete_specific_player_still_returns_204
preconditions: Player with squad_number=1 exists in the pre-loaded database
actions: Send HTTP DELETE to /players/squadnumber/1 using TestClient
expected: The specific sub-resource DELETE succeeds, proving 405 is path-specific to /players/ root
trace: R-PLAYER-036: 405 applies only to /players/ collection root, not to /players/squadnumber/{n}
Distinguishes global DELETE ban from path-specific 405
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_specific_player_still_returns_204():
    client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
    # Confirm DELETE on collection root is 405
    root_response = client.delete('/players/')
    assert root_response.status_code == 405, (
        f'Expected 405 on /players/ but got {root_response.status_code}'
    )
    # Confirm DELETE on specific resource is 204 (squad_number=1 exists in fixture)
    specific_response = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/1')
    assert specific_response.status_code == 204, (
        f'Expected 204 on /players/squadnumber/1 but got {specific_response.status_code}'
    )
    assert specific_response.status_code != 405
    assert specific_response.status_code != 404

test_delete_specific_player_still_returns_204()

tests.name: test_delete_players_root_response_body_indicates_method_not_allowed
preconditions: No DELETE route registered for /players/ collection
actions: Send HTTP DELETE to /players/ using TestClient
expected: Response body contains 'detail' key with value 'Method Not Allowed'
trace: R-PLAYER-036: 405 response body must carry FastAPI default detail message
Catches mutations that change status code constant or detail string
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_players_root_response_body_indicates_method_not_allowed():
    client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
    response = client.delete('/players/')
    assert response.status_code == 405
    try:
        body = response.json()
    except Exception as exc:
        raise AssertionError(f'Response body is not valid JSON: {exc}') from exc
    assert 'detail' in body, f'Expected "detail" key in body: {body}'
    assert body['detail'] == 'Method Not Allowed', (
        f'Expected detail="Method Not Allowed" but got: {body["detail"]}'
    )

test_delete_players_root_response_body_indicates_method_not_allowed()
